mainTopic: Who waves ביכורים and private שלמים: the כהן together with the owner, why the משנה cites רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and which owners join in the waving themselves
overview: This amud starts at the end of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's comparison between ביכורים and שלמים. His conclusion is that both the כהן and the owner wave: the כהן puts his hands under the owner's hands. The גמרא asks why the משנה names only him, when רבי יהודה also requires waving ביכורים and learns it from 'והנחתו'. רבא answers that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's פסוק comes first. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that he is an especially great authority. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה about waving a private שלמים. רב יהודה says every owner's offering needs תנופה, but only a male Jewish owner joins in the waving himself. A ברייתא learns from 'בני ישראל' that גוים and women do not wave. רבי יוסי explains that logic alone would not have kept them out, because a כהן can do the waving. A second ברייתא includes גרים and freed slaves from the word 'המקריב', and proves from 'ידיו תביאינה' that this word means the owner. The amud ends where it began: the כהן's hands go under the owner's hands and they wave together.

steps.title: The two-way comparison between ביכורים and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's comparison works both ways. From ביכורים we learn that a כהן waves, and from שלמים we learn that the owner waves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as here a priest is involved, so too there a priest. And just as there the owner is involved, so too here the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a comparison between ביכורים ("here") and the שלמים offering ("there"). Each case teaches something to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ביכורים the פסוק says the כהן takes the basket, so the שלמים waving also needs a כהן. With שלמים the פסוק says the owner's own hands bring it, so ביכורים also need the owner. The result is that both cases need both people.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Priest
The owner of the offering
There (the other case being compared)

phrases.english: Just as here, a priest
phrases.notes: "Here" is ביכורים, where the כהן takes the basket. "There" is the שלמים offering.

phrases.english: so too there, a priest
and just as there, the owner
so too here, the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כָּאן כֹּהֵן אַף לְהַלָּן כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's derivation, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving of both ביכורים and שלמים needs both a כהן and the owner.

steps.title: How both the כהן and the owner can wave together
steps.stepSummary: Both people take part at once: the כהן puts his hand under the owner's hands and waves.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The priest places his hand beneath the hands of the owner and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how two people can both do the waving. They hold the item together, with the כהן's hand underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 required both the כהן and the owner, which seems hard to do. The answer is one shared action. The owner holds the item, the כהן's hand goes under the owner's hands, and they wave it together.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (how can both things be true?)
Waves (does the תנופה)
The waving ceremony done with certain offerings

steps.whatToRemember: ביכורים are waved by the owner and the כהן together. The כהן's hand goes beneath the owner's hands.

phrases.english: How so?
The priest places his hand
beneath the hands of the owner and waves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the practical problem raised by Step 1's rule that both people must wave.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method that satisfies both requirements at once
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seems impossible for both the כהן and the owner to do one waving.
steps.terutzMaskana: They wave together, with the כהן's hand beneath the owner's hands.

steps.title: Why not also mention רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה cites only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב for waving ביכורים. רבי יהודה also requires waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה also say it follows רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: "And you shall place it" means waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. Why name only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב when רבי יהודה holds the same rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes it sound as if only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires waving ביכורים. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה reads the word "והנחתו" as waving. So the rule seems to have two sources, and the משנה should have mentioned both.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it also say (why didn't it also mention...?)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
"And you shall place it" (the word רבי יהודה reads as waving)

phrases.english: And let it also say
in accordance with the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"And you shall place it" — this is waving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the derivation itself to a question about how the משנה words its attribution.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to cite only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה also requires waving ביכורים, so naming only one תנא seems incomplete.

steps.title: Inside the ברייתא: maybe it means real placing?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself whether "והנחתו" might simply mean placing the basket down rather than waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say this means waving, or does it mean only placing?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the quoted ברייתא, רבי יהודה questions his own reading. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of "והנחתו" is "put it down," not "wave it." The ברייתא raises this reading on purpose so that it can rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say... or is it perhaps only...? (a standard way to test a reading)
Placing (setting down)

phrases.english: Do you say this is waving,
or is it only placing?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר זוֹ תְּנוּפָה אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַנָּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 3 by testing its reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "והנחתו" mean waving, or does it keep its plain meaning of placing?

steps.title: Placing is already written elsewhere, so this means waving
steps.stepSummary: An earlier פסוק already says the כהן places the basket. So the extra word "והנחתו" must be teaching waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says "and he shall place it," placing is already stated. So how do I fulfill "and you shall place it"? This is waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its reading. The Torah already mentions placing in an earlier פסוק, so the second mention must teach something new: waving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דברים 26:4 already says the כהן places the basket before the מזבח. If 26:10 also meant placing, it would say nothing new. So רבי יהודה reads it as a separate requirement of תנופה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is already stated
How do I fulfill (what does this extra word come to teach?)
"And he shall place it" (the כהן's placing in דברים 26:4)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה also requires waving ביכורים. He learns it from the extra "והנחתו" in דברים 26:10.

phrases.english: When it says "and he shall place it,"
phrases.notes: דברים 26:4, where the כהן puts the basket down before the מזבח.

phrases.english: placing is already stated;
so how do I fulfill "and you shall place it"?
This is waving.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר וְהִנִּיחוֹ הֲרֵי הַנָּחָה אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own question from Step 4, which completes the support for the קשיא in Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing is already taught in 26:4, so "והנחתו" in 26:10 must mean waving.

steps.title: רבא: his פסוק comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה chose רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because his source פסוק appears earlier in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because the verse opened with it first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question of Step 3. The משנה named רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because his פסוק comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns waving from "ולקח הכהן הטנא מידך" in 26:4. רבי יהודה learns it from 26:10, which comes later. The משנה cited the source that appears first in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
The פסוק opened with it first

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since it opened with it
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's פסוק (26:4), which comes before רבי יהודה's (26:10).

phrases.english: the verse, first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח בּוֹ הַכָּתוּב תְּחִלָּה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה chose one source over another, based on the order of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have named both תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It named רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because his פסוק comes earlier.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: he is a great authority
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another answer: the משנה named רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because of his great standing in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Because his strength is great.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. The משנה named רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because he is an especially great authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is about the person, not the order of the פסוקים. Because רבי אליעזר בן יעקב carries special weight, the משנה cited him alone.

keyTerms.meaning: His strength (authority) is great

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the משנה names רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבא: his פסוק comes first. רב נחמן בר יצחק: he is a great authority.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Since his strength is great.
phrases.notes: Literally "his manliness is great." He means רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is a weighty authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר הוֹאִיל וְרַב גֻּבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same קשיא that רבא answered in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the choice of source by the authority of the תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have named both תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It named רבי אליעזר בן יעקב because of his great Torah authority.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling on waving שלמים seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about waving the parts of a private שלמים and asks what it means, since the wording seems to contradict itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the altar parts of an individual's peace offerings, and their breast and thigh, are waved. This applies to both men and women, by Jews but not by others. The גמרא asks: what is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about waving a private שלמים. It then asks what the line means, because it seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the משנה says waving applies to 'both men and women.' Then it says 'by Jews but not by others,' which seems to leave women out. So the question 'מאי קאמר' is a real challenge: the two halves of the line do not seem to fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Peace offerings brought by one private person
The breast and thigh of a שלמים, which are given to the כהן
'What is it saying?' The גמרא uses this when a text seems unclear or self-contradictory

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אחד האנשים ואחד הנשים' and 'בישראל אבל לא באחרים' as two separate lists. The whole difficulty is that the second half seems to cancel the first.

phrases.english: And the sacrificial portions of an individual's peace offerings,
and their breast and thigh,
phrases.notes: The משנה means that all of these parts need waving.

phrases.english: both men and women,
by Jews but not by others.
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of ביכורים to the next ruling in the משנה, about שלמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording about who is included in תנופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Including women and then saying 'only ישראל, not others' looks like an internal contradiction.

steps.title: Women's offerings are waved, but women do not do the waving
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that every owner's offering needs תנופה, but only a male Jewish owner joins in the waving himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this is what the משנה means. For both men and women, their offering needs waving. But the waving itself is done by Jewish men, and not by women.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by splitting the משנה's line into two separate rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Men and women' answers whose offering needs waving: everyone's does. 'Jews, not others' answers who does the waving with his own hands: a male Jewish owner, and not a woman. So the משנה is talking about two different things, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means.' Used to introduce an explanation of a confusing text
Requires waving
By the hands of women

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer separates two questions: whether an offering needs a מצוה done to it, and who is allowed to do that מצוה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
both men and women,
their offering requires waving,
and the waving itself is by Jews,
phrases.notes: He means Jewish men. The male owner waves together with the כהן.

phrases.english: but not by the hands of women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the line is read as two separate rulings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed both to include and to exclude women in תנופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women's offerings do need תנופה, but only a male Jewish owner takes part in the waving itself.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman's שלמים is waved, but she does not wave it herself.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Jewish men wave, but not גוים or women
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'בני ישראל' that גוים and women do not wave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Children of Israel' wave, and gentiles do not wave. 'Sons of Israel' wave, and women do not wave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the Torah source for who does the waving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns two things from the same phrase 'בני ישראל.' The word 'ישראל' leaves out גוים. The word 'בני,' which can mean 'sons,' leaves out women. This fits רב יהודה's reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They wave (do תנופה)
Non-Jews
Children, or sons, of Israel. Here the phrase is read both ways

phrases.english: The Sages taught: The children of Israel wave,
phrases.notes: The source is ויקרא 7:29: 'Speak to the children of Israel...'

phrases.english: and gentiles do not wave.
The sons of Israel wave,
phrases.notes: Same words read a second way: "בני" as "sons," meaning men.

phrases.english: and women do not wave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the rule that only male Jews do the waving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'בני ישראל': גוים and women do not wave.

steps.title: Should the placing-hands distinction apply to waving too?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי notes that the Torah separates Jews, גוים and women for סמיכה, and asks whether we should separate them for תנופה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: We find that the Torah separated the offering of a Jew from the offering of gentiles and the offering of women regarding placing hands. Could we also separate them regarding waving?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי begins a new line of thought. He raises a possible comparison between סמיכה and תנופה and asks whether it holds. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For סמיכה, the Torah already treats the offerings of a male Jew, a גוי, and a woman differently. רבי יוסי suggests that we might apply the same split to תנופה. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner pressing his hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
'We have found.' Used to bring a known example from elsewhere
The Torah made a distinction
'One might think.' Introduces a possible idea that is about to be checked

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
We have found that the verse distinguished
between the offering of a Jew and the offering of gentiles
and the offering of women, regarding placing hands;
might we distinguish regarding waving?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new comparison to סמיכה to check the scope of the rules about תנופה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the distinctions the Torah makes for סמיכה also apply to תנופה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains why logic would not separate them for waving
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers his own question: no. סמיכה is special because only the owner can do it, but תנופה can be done by כהנים, so logic gives no reason to leave anyone out.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Why did the Torah separate them for סמיכה? Because סמיכה must be done by the owner himself. Should we separate them for תנופה too? Waving is done by the כהנים, so there is no reason to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers the question from Step 11 by saying 'no': we cannot simply copy the סמיכה rule over to תנופה. This sets up his next point about why the פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the owner himself can do סמיכה, and he cannot send someone else in his place. So if גוים and women cannot do it, it makes sense that their offerings skip it. תנופה is different, because a כהן can do the waving, so on logic alone everyone's offering could be waved.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it that... / what is the reason that...
By the owners themselves (no one can do it for them)
By the כהנים

phrases.english: No. Why did it differentiate with regard to leaning?
phrases.notes: "It" is the Torah, which treated Jews, גוים and women differently for סמיכה.

phrases.english: Because leaning is done by the owners.
Should we differentiate with regard to waving,
when waving is done by priests?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's question from Step 11 by rejecting the comparison between סמיכה and תנופה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the separation of Jews, גוים and women for סמיכה should carry over to תנופה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. סמיכה depends on the owner alone, but תנופה can be done by כהנים, so logic would not separate them.

steps.title: So the verse is needed to leave out גוים and women
steps.stepSummary: Since logic would include everyone, the words 'בני ישראל' must be coming to teach that גוים and women do not wave.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'בני ישראל'? To teach that Jews wave and גוים do not wave, and that Jewish men wave and women do not wave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי concludes that the פסוק's words are what leave out גוים and women from תנופה. Logic alone would not have left them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because logic would have included everyone, the words 'בני ישראל' would have no job unless they come to exclude. The word 'ישראל' leaves out גוים, and 'בני', meaning 'sons', leaves out women.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
If so (draws the result of the previous argument)

steps.whatToRemember: גוים and women are kept from doing the waving themselves only because the פסוק says so. Logic alone would not have separated them, since a כהן can do the waving.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means a woman's offering is not waved at all. As רב יהודה explained in Step 9, her offering is waved. The פסוק only teaches that she does not join in the waving herself.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse state 'the children of Israel'?
The children of Israel wave,
but the gentiles do not wave.
The sons of Israel wave,
but the women do not wave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from Step 12: since logic would include everyone, the פסוק must be what excludes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The words 'בני ישראל' teach that גוים and women do not do the waving themselves. Logic alone, based on the כהן's role, would not have excluded them.

steps.title: Another ברייתא includes converts and freed slaves
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא asks how we know that גרים and freed slaves also wave, and learns it from the word 'המקריב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'בני ישראל' would only tell me about people born Jewish. How do I know that גרים and freed slaves are included? The פסוק says 'המקריב', 'the one who brings'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same פסוק. It shows that converts and freed slaves are also obligated in תנופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בני ישראל' might sound like they mean only people born Jewish. The extra word 'המקריב', meaning anyone who brings the offering, widens the rule to include גרים and freed slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Converts
Freed (non-Jewish) slaves
From where do we know?

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita: 'The children of Israel':
I have only the children of Israel.
From where do we know converts and freed slaves?
The verse states: 'He who offers.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:כט. This word comes right after 'בני ישראל' in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא on the same פסוק, this time including people rather than excluding them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גרים and freed slaves are also obligated in תנופה, learned from the word 'המקריב'.

steps.title: Maybe 'the one who brings' means the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own reading: maybe 'המקריב' refers to the כהן who brings the offering on the מזבח, not to converts and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'המקריב' means the כהן who brings the offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions the reading it just gave. It suggests a different meaning for the word 'המקריב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'המקריב' could easily describe the כהן, since he is the one who actually offers on the מזבח. If so, the word would not come to include גרים and slaves at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it only means...
The כהן who offers the קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא זֶה כֹּהֵן הַמַּקְרִיב?
phrases.english: Or perhaps this is only the priest who offers?

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'המקריב' as the owner, which includes גרים and freed slaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as well refer to the כהן, so it would not prove anything about converts and slaves.

steps.title: The next verse shows the owner is meant
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the next פסוק, 'his own hands shall bring', clearly speaks about the owner, so 'המקריב' is the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'his own hands shall bring', it is talking about the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back the challenge by pointing to the very next פסוק. That פסוק shows the subject is the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His own hands shall bring' means the person whose offering it is brings it himself. Since that פסוק continues the same subject, 'המקריב' must also be the owner, and that is why it can include גרים and freed slaves.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the context of the next פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'המקריב' might mean the כהן who offers on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The next פסוק speaks of the owner's own hands, so the owner is the one the פסוקים are talking about.

steps.title: How the owner and the כהן wave together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how this works in practice. The כהן places his hands under the owner's hands, and they wave together.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this done? The כהן puts his hands under the owner's hands and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how the owner can wave if a כהן is also part of the waving. It then describes how the two do it together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the owner's own hands, yet a כהן also has a role in the waving. The solution has both of them hold the parts at once: the owner's hands on top and the כהן's hands underneath.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How does this work?
He waves

steps.whatToRemember: For a private שלמים, a male Jewish owner (including a גר or freed slave) waves together with the כהן. The כהן's hands go under the owner's hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how Step 9's rule plays out in practice: every offering gets תנופה, and the owner joins in himself.
